title: High-Pressure NIV with moderate backup-frequency and expiratory ramp – a prospective observational study
summary: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) can lead to severe respiratory failure. One method of treating respiratory failure is non-invasive ventilation via a mask, which relieves the respiratory muscles. The settings of the HP-NIV-MER are based on the specific characteristics of the lungs of COPD patients. This study aims to show that respiratory failure can be treated with the HP-NIV-MER and that acceptance among severely affected patients is high.

interventions.name: The study aims to demonstrate the effectiveness of HP-NIV-MER based on the analysis of retrospective and prospective routine data. Patients with COPD are treated with HP-NIV-MER at our hospital. Accordingly, routine data is collected at the time of initiation and at the first follow-up examination,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure
HP-NIV-MER
Exclusion criteria:
Lung and thoracic diseases others than COPD
Severe obesity (BMI greater than 35 kg/m2)
Severe heart failure, unstable angina, or severe arrhythmias
Malignant underlying or concomitant disease
Inability to attend the first follow-up after approximately 3 months
Acute hypercapnia with acidosis and/or aeCOPD
